doc.title: Marty Sheller interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 9, 2022

title: Jon Hendricks and the unrecorded lyrics to 'Cuidado'
summary: Hendricks wrote lyrics to Sheller's solo, recorded a scratch version, took an advance and moved to Europe.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. When you mentioned Jon Hendricks, that brings a story to mind again about Mongo. I had written a song called “Cuidado” which means be careful, and it was an uptempo mambo, a jazz mambo, written basically on bebop kind of chords. And Mongo was with Columbia at that time. And somehow Jon Hendricks wrote lyrics to my solo that I played on that. And we were going into the studio to record so Mongo said, “Hey Jon, come to the studio and record that, it sounds great. It’ll be a great selling point.” So he came into the studio, put him in a booth, and boy did he sound good. He really sounded terrific. So Mongo said, “Great, that’ll be on the record.” Jon said, “No, no, no. I can do a much better version. That was just the scratch version.” Mongo said, “No, no, I mean it’s great.” And Jon insisted no, that it was just temporary. So Jon got an advance from Columbia Records, which I’m not sure what it was but I’m sure it must have been a nice taste. He still had a great reputation at that point and all. And Jon disappeared. He moved to Europe and we never had an opportunity to do it. And it was always in my mind and Mongo said the same thing, that he didn’t — it sounded so good, what he had written — and you know the way he was he was like very particular about doing it right, about using the right syllables and putting lyrics to it. And he did a great job, but we never had an opportunity to record it with him. Who knows whatever happened to that tape.
